messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
A good rule of thumb for U.S. homes is roughly **5 kWh per square foot per year** (though this can vary by climate, insulation, and lifestyle).  
For a 2,000 sq ft house that would be about:

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Annual consumption | ≈ 10,000 kWh |
| Monthly average | ≈ 833 kWh |
| Daily average | ≈ 27 kWh |

If you’re looking to size a solar system, you’d need to factor in your local average sunlight hours and any efficiency losses. For example, if you get 5 hrs/day of peak sun, a 10 kW system (≈ 30 panels) would produce roughly 13,000 kWh/year, which would cover that 10,000 kWh demand with some surplus.

Let me know if you’d like a quick calculation for your exact location (sun hours, panel efficiency, etc.) or if you have other questions!
